title.narrative: Providing emergency life-saving access to safe, clean water, sanitation, and hygiene to climate shock affected IDP and host communities in Dinsoor district.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtREADO will deliver emergency water, sanitation, and hygiene services to 15,972 drought-affected people across Dinsoor’s IDP and host communities in urban and rural areas, combining life-saving response with sustainable solutions. READO will construct 55 flood-proof VIP latrines and build 5 fully accessible, disability-inclusive units mount 40 environmental sanitation campaigns alongside 40 participatory hygiene-promotion sessions and distribute hygiene kits to 2,662 of the most vulnerable households. At the same time, READO will restore reliable clean-water access by rehabilitating 8 strategically located shallow wells, serving up to 4,000 individuals in IDP sites and host community villages, then establish routine chlorination protocols and train local Water Management Committees in operation, maintenance, and water-safety planning. Finally, community-led solid-waste management initiatives will reduce health risks and protect the environment, ensuring that WASH gains are both immediate and lasting. READO will coordinate with the FSC, CCCM, WASH, and Nutrition partners to avoid duplication/overlapping of activities in Dinsoor. Furthermore, in line with the SHF Allocation Strategy, READO will ensure convergence through joint community mobilisation, beneficiary selection, which will not only ensure maximum integration with other sectors (Health, Nutrition and FSL) but limit inclusion and exclusion errors. READO in coordination with OCHA will organise a meeting with all SHF partners in Dinsoor to ensure convergence. ltbrgtFurthermore, this project will ensure protection mainstreaming by prioritising the safety, dignity, and equitable access of all beneficiaries throughout program design and implementation. Activities will be planned with community participation to identify and mitigate risks, avoid harm, and address barriers faced by marginalized groups. Disability inclusion will be integral, with tailored work roles and accommodations ensuring persons with disabilities can participate safely and meaningfully. The beneficiary selection criteria and targeting processes will actively include women, youth, the elderly, and people with disabilities to prevent exclusion. Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be embedded across all activities through staff training, strict codes of conduct, PDM questions, and clear contractual clauses with suppliers. READO confidential, accessible feedback and complaint mechanisms will enable beneficiaries to report concerns safely. PSEA awareness materials will be widely displayed, and a dedicated focal point will monitor and respond to risks promptly. ltbrgtREADO has a strong presence in Southwest State and has implemented Food Security and WASH projects in Dinsoor previously, hence bearing operational capacity to directly implement. In addition, READO has a strong knowledge of the local context and developed a good rapport with the local administration and communities. Through this 12-month WASH project in Dinsoor, READO hopes to build on this good rapport with the community and be in a position to respond quickly to the needs of the target locations. In addition, READO has the added advantage of being an LNGO, and it implements its activities through local staff with high knowledge and experience Somalia's context and clan dynamics. READO will ensure community engagement in all phases of the project, particularly women's participation and will conduct community sensitization on the project's scope and the expected outcomes. ltbrgtThe following are the target locations among the IDP and host communities in Dinsoor: Sawure, Easow, Tuni, Abdalla Hassan, Ala dacar-hilac, Billow alla, Haja nina, Alinoor Ali Barakowltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
